channel.title: The FIG blog
channel.description: Restaurant deals in Markham, Ontario, and ideas for independent restaurants.

item.title: Owner, Manager or Staff: setting up your team and sign-in security on FIG
item.description: Who should hold which role on FIG, how people join by invite, which steps need a stronger sign-in, and how to set it up so a busy shift runs smoothly and the money steps stay with the right people.

item.title: Reading your FIG Payments page: takeout, fees and your bookkeeping
item.description: Every takeout payment, refund and fee is listed on one page and downloads as a CSV file. How to read it, what each line means, a worked month-end example with the sums checked, and how to hand it to your bookkeeper.

item.title: Replying to reviews: a short guide for restaurant owners
item.description: How to answer a review in a few minutes a week: what to say to a good review, a bad one and a rating with no words, with templates you can adapt and a little arithmetic on what one low rating does.

item.title: Takeout or dine-in with a deal: which costs you less?
item.description: The same dish can cost different amounts depending on how you eat it. A side-by-side of dine-in and takeout with a deal, with the HST, the drink, the tip and the trip worked out.

item.title: Family dinner out in Markham for less: a plan for four, with the math
item.description: Eating out with kids does not have to cost a lot. How to pick an early table, choose the deal that fits a family of four, check the sums with HST and keep the extras in check.

item.title: Takeout during a rush: pause, prep time and deals per order
item.description: Takeout should fill the kitchen in quiet hours, not hurt the dining room at your peak. How to use pause, prep time and deals per order on FIG, with a simple capacity sum.

item.title: Date night in Markham for less: a plan, with the math
item.description: A dinner out for two does not have to cost a lot. How to pick the hour, choose the deal that fits the two of you, check the sums with HST and plan a walk afterwards.

item.title: Deal not working at the counter? What to check and what to say
item.description: A code that will not scan, a deal that seems to be over, a pickup that went wrong: the usual reasons a FIG deal does not apply at the counter, what to try first, and how to ask politely.

item.title: Eating out with dietary needs or allergies: filters, calling ahead and what to ask
item.description: Halal, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free or an allergy: how to use diet filters as a starting point, and what to ask a restaurant before you go and when you order.

item.title: Train your staff to honour a FIG deal in 10 minutes
item.description: A deal only works if the person at the counter knows what to do with it. A ten-minute training plan for restaurant staff: how to scan, what to check, what to say when something looks off, and a one-page cheat sheet.

item.title: Is it a good deal? How to compare restaurant deals
item.description: 2-for-1, 20% off, $3 off or a free drink: which one saves you the most? A plain method for comparing restaurant deals, with worked examples, so you pick the one that fits what you were going to eat anyway.

item.title: Takeout order math: what a restaurant keeps on a $12, $20, $40 or $60 order
item.description: On FIG, takeout paid in the app costs 5% of the food plus Stripe's card fee. The $0.30 part of that fee is fixed, so small orders cost a bigger share. Here are the numbers on four order sizes, and what to do about them.

item.title: How restaurant deals work on FIG, from claim to counter
item.description: Everything that happens between seeing a deal and paying the bill: claiming, your Deals page, the code at the counter, takeout, what happens when a deal ends, and rating the visit.

item.title: How to run a slow-hour deal that makes money (with the math)
item.description: A slow-hour deal makes money when it fills seats that would otherwise be empty and covers its food cost. Here's the arithmetic: contribution per plate, the worst case, the cap, and how to tell new diners from regulars who'd have come anyway.

item.title: % off, $ off or 2-for-1? Pricing a restaurant deal
item.description: The four kinds of restaurant deal, side by side: what each costs you, what it feels like to a diner, and when to use it. With worked examples on a $14 dish.

item.title: Set up your FIG menu and takeout in 15 minutes
item.description: A step-by-step guide for restaurant owners: your page, your menu, your first deal, and in-app takeout with your HST number and Stripe payouts, explained simply.

item.title: HST registration for small restaurants in Ontario: the $30,000 rule explained
item.description: When a small Ontario restaurant has to register for HST, what changes when it does, and how HST works on deals and takeout. Plain-language, with the Canada Revenue Agency's own rules linked.

item.title: Eating out as a group: picking a place, deals and splitting the bill
item.description: How to get a group from 'where should we eat?' to a table: deciding fast, checking there's room, making deals work for everyone, and splitting the bill fairly, with the arithmetic.

item.title: How to read a restaurant's reviews on FIG
item.description: Reviews on FIG come only from diners whose visit was scanned. Here's how ratings, likes and replies work, and how to read a restaurant's page to decide in a minute.

item.title: How FIG makes money: 5% of in-app takeout
item.description: FIG is free for restaurants, with no commission on dine-in and no fee per diner. FIG earns only on takeout orders diners pay for in the app: it keeps 5% of the food.

item.title: How to find the best restaurant deals in Markham
item.description: A practical guide to eating out for less in Markham, Ontario: when restaurants post deals, where to look across the city, and how to use FIG to find and use them.

item.title: Delivery app commissions vs FIG: what restaurants keep
item.description: Delivery apps charge restaurants a percentage of every order. FIG is free for restaurants on dine-in, with nothing per diner, and keeps 5% of the food on in-app takeout. Here are the published Canadian rates and what a restaurant keeps from the same order.

item.title: 7 ways to fill slow hours at your restaurant
item.description: Practical, low-cost ways for independent restaurants to bring in diners on quiet afternoons and weeknights, with the arithmetic to make sure a deal adds money instead of giving it away.

item.title: Student food deals in Markham: eating out on a budget
item.description: How high school and university students in Markham can eat out for less: when deals show up, how to set a real budget, how to decide as a group, and how FIG keeps it free.

item.title: What are flash deals, and how do they work on FIG?
item.description: Flash deals are short, real-time restaurant deals posted during unexpected quiet spells. Here's how they work for diners and restaurants, how to catch them, and what happens to a claim when the timer ends.

item.title: Takeout with a deal, pick up, skip the delivery fees
item.description: Some FIG deals let you order takeout from a Markham restaurant's menu and pick it up yourself, with no delivery or service fees. Here's how it works, what it costs, and what happens if you're late.

item.title: Why we built FIG
item.description: Markham is full of great independent restaurants, and most of them run on thin margins. FIG is a deals app built around that: free for diners and for restaurants, with no cut of a dine-in bill.
